info.title: JointFM inference service
info.description:
The HTTP contract of a `jointfm-inference` service. `GET /healthz` reports what the service serves and the limits a request must keep; `POST /predict` answers forecast and condition queries over one table of rows. Every prediction request names the contract version in `schema_version`, and this document describes the version in `info.version`. An unknown path answers 404 with an `ErrorResponse`.

The service generates this document from its own code (`jointfm-inference schema`).

servers.description: A local service on its default port.

post.summary: Answer a forecast or condition query
post.description: Answers a `PredictRequest` with a `PredictResponse`, and a `HealthRequest` with the `HealthResponse` of `GET /healthz`.

400.description: The request is malformed, asks for something the service does not serve, names a version it does not speak, or asks for more samples than `max_sample_count`.

408.description: The request body stopped arriving before `Content-Length` bytes came.

413.description: `Content-Length` exceeds `max_request_bytes`; the body is not read.

500.description: The service failed on a request it accepted.

PredictRequest.description: A forecast or condition query over one table of rows. Rules that depend on the modes are listed under `allOf`.

request_type.description: `predict`, the default. A request whose `request_type` is `health` is a `HealthRequest` instead.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract the request speaks; any other is refused with `SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH`.

model_version.description: When set, the service refuses the request with `MODEL_VERSION_MISMATCH` unless it serves exactly this `model_version`, as `/healthz` reports it.

query_mode.description:
What the request asks of the distribution; defaults to `forecast`.

- `forecast`: The joint distribution of the columns at each future position, given the history.
- `condition`: The same, additionally conditioned at the positions `conditions` covers on pinned values or bands of some columns; a position no condition covers answers as in `forecast`. Served only where `/healthz` lists it in `supported_query_modes`.

return_mode.description:
What the response carries; defaults to `mean`. `/healthz` lists the modes a service serves in `supported_return_modes`.

- `mean`: The mean of each requested column at each future position.
- `samples`: `n_samples` draws from the joint distribution, each covering every future position and requested column.
- `quantiles`: The marginal quantiles at the levels `quantiles` lists, per future position and requested column.
- `log_prob`: The joint log density of the observed `query_rows` at each future position.

time_index_mode.description:
How the request's times read. `/healthz` lists the modes a service serves in `supported_time_index_modes`.

- `ordinal`: Times are integer steps of a regular grid. Without `time_column`, history rows sit at steps `0` to `rows - 1`.
- `continuous_float`: Times are real numbers in the column `time_column` names.
- `absolute_datetime`: Times are ISO 8601 timestamps in the column `time_column` names.

time_column.description: The row key holding each row's time; it must not name a declared column. Required unless `time_index_mode` is `ordinal`.

time_scale_seconds.description: Seconds per time unit the model reads `absolute_datetime` times in; defaults to 31557600, one Julian year.

timezone.description: The IANA zone name, such as `Europe/Berlin`, of the `absolute_datetime` timestamps; it must match the zone the timestamps carry, if any.

columns.description: The columns of every row, in the order the response reports them by default. More columns than `/healthz` reports as `data_generation.max_series` are refused with `INPUT_SIZE_EXCEEDED`.

requested_columns.description: The columns the response carries, in this order, each by name or by zero-based index into `columns`; omitted or `null`, every declared column in declared order. A `log_prob` request names every declared column in declared order or omits the field.

history_rows.description: The observed rows, in strictly increasing time order. Each holds a finite number for every declared column and, when `time_column` is set, the row's time.

query_times.description: The future times to answer, strictly increasing and after the last history time: ISO 8601 timestamps for `absolute_datetime`, numbers otherwise. Each is one future position of the response.

query_rows.description: Read only, and required, for `log_prob`: the observed row at each query time, in `query_times` order, with a finite value for every declared column and, when `time_column` is set, its query time.

conditions.description: Required for, and allowed only with, `query_mode` `condition`. A column carries at most one condition per position, and every position keeps at least one column unconditioned.

n_samples.description: The number of draws behind `samples` and behind any answer the service estimates by sampling. Defaults to the service's `max_sample_count`, which `/healthz` reports and no request may exceed (`INPUT_SIZE_EXCEEDED`).

quantiles.description: Read only, and required, for `quantiles`: the levels, each strictly between 0 and 1, in the order the response reports them.

seed.description: Seeds the service's random draws. The same request with the same seed returns the same answer while `/healthz` reports the same `checkpoint_version`, `image_version`, `device`, and `precision`. `requested_columns` only selects among the draws, so changing it leaves the columns still returned unchanged; changing anything else, `n_samples` included, can change every draw. Omitted or `null`, draws differ per request.

HealthRequest.description: Asks for the `/healthz` payload through `POST /predict`. The service reads no other field.

name.description: The column's name, unique among `columns`: the key of its value in each row and the name the response reports it under.

role.description:
What the column is to the caller; defaults to `feature`.

- `target`: A column the caller cares about forecasting.
- `feature`: A column that informs the forecast. The model forecasts every column whatever its role.

lower_bound.description: A lower bound every sampled draw of the column respects; at most `upper_bound`. Read only for `samples`: a draw outside the bound is replaced by a fresh draw, across all columns of its position at once, so the draws follow the joint distribution restricted to the bounds. A bound that draws still miss after 100 redraws is refused with `VALIDATION_ERROR` on this field.

upper_bound.description: An upper bound every sampled draw of the column respects. Read only for `samples`: a draw outside the bound is replaced by a fresh draw, across all columns of its position at once, so the draws follow the joint distribution restricted to the bounds. A bound that draws still miss after 100 redraws is refused with `VALIDATION_ERROR` on this field.

Row.description: One row: a value per declared column, keyed by the column's name, and the row's time under `time_column`. Other keys are ignored.

EqualityCondition.description: Pins one column to one value at the covered positions.

column.description: The name of the declared column the condition applies to.

value.description: The finite value the column is pinned to.

query_time_indices.description: Zero-based indices into `query_times` of the future positions the condition covers; `null` covers every position.

IntervalCondition.description: Confines one column to a band at the covered positions.

column.description: The name of the declared column the condition applies to.

lower.description: The band's finite lower end, below `upper`; `null` leaves it open.

upper.description: The band's finite upper end; `null` leaves it open. A band open on both sides conditions nothing and is refused.

query_time_indices.description: Zero-based indices into `query_times` of the future positions the condition covers; `null` covers every position.

PredictResponse.description: The answer to a prediction request, one variant per return mode.

return_mode.description: The request's return mode, which decides the variant.

plausibility.description: How plausible a `condition` query's conditions are under the forecast; `null` for `forecast` queries.

query_times.description: The request's `query_times`, one per future position: ISO 8601 strings for `absolute_datetime`, numbers otherwise.

requested_columns.description: The names of the columns the answer covers, in its column order.

mean.description: Indexed `[position][column]`: the mean of each requested column at each future position.

return_mode.description: The request's return mode, which decides the variant.

plausibility.description: How plausible a `condition` query's conditions are under the forecast; `null` for `forecast` queries.

query_times.description: The request's `query_times`, one per future position: ISO 8601 strings for `absolute_datetime`, numbers otherwise.

requested_columns.description: The names of the columns the answer covers, in its column order.

return_mode.description: The request's return mode, which decides the variant.

plausibility.description: How plausible a `condition` query's conditions are under the forecast; `null` for `forecast` queries.

query_times.description: The request's `query_times`, one per future position: ISO 8601 strings for `absolute_datetime`, numbers otherwise.

requested_columns.description: The names of the columns the answer covers, in its column order.

quantiles.description: One entry per requested level, in request order.

return_mode.description: The request's return mode, which decides the variant.

plausibility.description: How plausible a `condition` query's conditions are under the forecast; `null` for `forecast` queries.

query_times.description: The request's `query_times`, one per future position: ISO 8601 strings for `absolute_datetime`, numbers otherwise.

requested_columns.description: The names of the columns the answer covers, in its column order.

log_prob.description: The log density of the observed `query_rows`.

values.description: Indexed `[position][column]`: the level's quantile of each requested column at each future position.

LogProbScores.description: The log density of the observed rows, per position and summed.

values.description: The joint log density of the observed row at each future position.

Plausibility.description: How plausible the conditions are under the forecast.

equality_log_density.description: The joint log density of every pinned value under the forecast, summed over positions; `null` without equality conditions.

region_log_probability.description: The log probability of every band under the forecast given the pinned values, summed over positions; `null` without interval conditions. Its sum with `equality_log_density` is the plausibility of the whole condition set; only differences between comparable requests carry meaning.

history_rows.description: The number of history rows read.

horizon_count.description: The number of future positions answered.

history_rows.description: The number of history rows read.

horizon_count.description: The number of future positions answered.

condition_draws.description: The draws behind each conditioned position's answer.

interval_estimator.description: The estimate behind the band probability at the position whose estimate is least supported; `null` unless some position bands more than one column.

IntervalEstimator.description: The estimate behind a multi-column band probability.

points.description: Quasi-random points per mixture component behind the estimate.

effective_sample_size.description: Kish's effective sample size of the estimate's importance weights; far below `points`, the estimate is unreliable.

HealthResponse.description: What the service serves and the limits a request must keep.

status.description: `ok` once the service has loaded its checkpoint and serves requests.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract the service speaks, which every prediction request sends.

model_version.description: Identifies the served model; a request may send it to be refused after the service changes models.

checkpoint_version.description: A label for the served checkpoint, by default the start of its SHA-256 digest.

checkpoint_path.description: Where the service reads the checkpoint file.

device.description: The device every model forward runs on, such as `cpu` or `cuda`.

precision.description:
The precision every model forward runs at.

- `fp32`: Every operation runs in float32.
- `bf16`: Matrix products and attention run in bfloat16 under automatic mixed precision; numerically sensitive operations stay in float32.
- `fp16`: As `bf16`, in float16.

generation.description: The generation of the served checkpoint, such as `jointfm-1`.

head.description: The kind of the served model's output head.

tail_map.description: The per-column tail map the head's forecast applies, or `none`.

decoding_strategy.description: How the served model decodes future positions. A JointFM 1 model reports `parallel_dense`: one forward emits the joint distribution of every position, and each position is drawn on its own, so a draw is joint across the columns of a position and independent across positions.

supported_query_modes.description: The query modes the service answers.

supported_condition_kinds.description: The condition kinds a `condition` query may use.

supported_return_modes.description: The return modes the service answers.

supported_time_index_modes.description: The time-index modes the service reads.

time_index_encoding.description:
How the served model reads time.

- `discrete_grid`: The model reads time as integer steps of a regular grid.

max_sample_count.description: The largest `n_samples` a request may ask for, and its default.

max_request_bytes.description: The largest request body, in bytes, the service reads; a larger one is refused unread with `INPUT_SIZE_EXCEEDED`.

max_concurrent_requests.description: How many prediction requests the service runs at once; further ones wait for a free slot.

data_generation.description: The request sizes the served model was built for.

CapacityEnvelope.description: The request sizes the served model was built for, so a client can size and split its requests.

min_series.description: The fewest columns a training sample of the model carried. It describes the training data and limits no request: one column is enough.

max_series.description: The most columns the model was built for, and the most one request may declare.

t_input.description: The time span of the longest history the model was built for.

t_output.description: The time span of the furthest horizon the model was built for.

n_input.description: The longest history the model was built for, in steps.

n_output.description: The longest horizon the model was built for, in steps.

Error.description: One reason the service refused or failed a request.

code.description:
What went wrong, as a value a client can branch on.

- `VALIDATION_ERROR`: The request is malformed, asks for something the service does not serve, or asks for values the forecast puts almost no probability on, such as draws inside a column bound far from it; `field` names the offending field.
- `UNSUPPORTED_HEAD_QUERY_COMBINATION`: In the catalog but not sent by this service: the mounted head answers every `query_mode`.
- `UNSUPPORTED_RETURN_MODE`: In the catalog but not sent by this service: an unserved `return_mode` answers `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
- `INPUT_SIZE_EXCEEDED`: The request exceeds a service cap: `n_samples` above `max_sample_count`, more `columns` than `data_generation.max_series`, or a body above `max_request_bytes`. `requested` and `allowed` carry both sizes.
- `SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH`: `schema_version` differs from the version the service speaks.
- `MODEL_VERSION_MISMATCH`: `model_version` differs from the version the service serves.
- `INTERNAL_ERROR`: The service failed on a request it accepted.

field.description: The request field or header the error is about, such as `columns[0].modality` or `Content-Length`; `null` when it concerns none.

requested.description: The size the request asked for, in the unit of `field`: samples for `n_samples`, columns for `columns`, bytes for `Content-Length`.

allowed.description: The largest size the service accepts, in the same unit.

ErrorResponse.description: The body of every non-200 response.

schema_version.description: The version of this contract the service speaks.

errors.description: Why the request was refused or failed.
